name: kg_readonly_oram_160k_temi_v2
status: completed end-to-end MP-SPDZ Temi execution with exact reconstruction
scope_warning: One favorable degree-one synthetic query, three parties on one localhost, preprocessing and 6.08 GB of externally prepared epoch shares. The read path is sublinear in logical records, but loading a fresh read-only epoch remains linear. This is not a persistent/update ORAM, LAN/WAN result, full MetaQA/WebQSP evaluation, malicious-security result, or production-scalability claim.

protocol.name: owner-built recursive read-only tree ORAM composed with MP-SPDZ Temi
protocol.security: static semi-honest adversary corrupting up to two of exactly three computation servers, conditional on the MP-SPDZ Temi backend claim
protocol.epoch_rule: fresh independently randomized owner trees and fresh 3-of-3 shares; each server atomically consumes the epoch once

oram_shape_per_owner.placement_conditioning_bound: at most 2^-80 across a stack by binary-KL Chernoff and union bounds

compiler.previous_field_major_attempt: interrupted after more than 12.7 million lines

offline_epoch_preparation.centralized_fixture_warning: The benchmark preparer reads all plaintext owners on one host. Deployment uses the independent per-owner shard writer; the centralized utility is not evidence of owner separation.

controlled_comparison_to_relation_paged_.interpretation: ORAM reduces cryptographic multiplication/communication but loses badly on latency because full fresh-state input and high-round recursive access dominate. It is not currently the best practical backend.

claim_boundary: Executable sublinear secret-dependent lookup inside a bounded fresh read-only epoch, composed with contribution-hiding two-hop KG retrieval and client-only top-k. End-to-end epoch setup remains linear and the system is semi-honest only.
